title: Ancient Trees in Slovakia: Cities to Explore
meta_description: Slovakia's national tree is the lime: its oldest linden, over 700 years, is tied by legend to a king's visit. Five places mapped, 11 trees.
intro: Slovakia's oldest trees are lindens, and that is not a coincidence: the lime is the country's national tree, on its coat of arms since the 13th century. Bojnice's linden, tied by local tradition to King Matthias Corvinus visiting the castle behind it, is put at over 700 years; Myjava's holds a documented 620; Kopcany's stands beside a Great Moravian-era church from the 10th century, one of the oldest buildings in the country. Bratislava's own collection reads almost as an inventory of other continents: a Japanese pagoda tree on the Danube embankment, an Empress tree from China in a small park, a paper birch that belongs in Canada, an Adriatic oak more at home on the Balkan coast. Kremnica's oak, national Tree of the Year in 2013, grows in a protected historic town garden with three more register trees still to verify nearby. 11 trees across five places, and the oldest by far still stands behind the castle where legend says it already did.
